architecture-avoid-boolean-props.notes: Mode booleans from the Incorrect example (isThread, isDMThread, isEditing, isForwarding) must be gone. Renamed booleans (e.g. `editing: boolean`) are not caught; read eval output for those.

architecture-compound-components.notes: Incorrect uses render-slot props and show-boolean props. Correct exposes the parts on one compound object or as named exports (the Server Components note).

patterns-children-over-render-props.notes: Incorrect passes render functions (renderHeader, renderFooter, renderActions) and invokes them. Correct takes children.

patterns-explicit-variants.notes: Incorrect is one <Composer> with boolean flags. Correct names each variant as its own component (<ThreadComposer>, <EditMessageComposer>). The capital-letter prefix means bare <Composer> does not count.

react19-ref-as-prop-and-use.notes: Incorrect wraps a component in forwardRef. Correct takes ref as a plain prop (React 19). forwardRef is still valid in React 18 code, so the rule is only applied to React 19-only code.

state-context-interface.notes: Incorrect couples the UI to one provider-specific hook. Correct reads the generic interface through useComposer().

state-decouple-implementation.notes: Incorrect UI component calls the implementation hooks directly. Correct moves them into a Provider; the UI only uses Composer parts.

state-lift-state.notes: Incorrect keeps useState inside a *Composer component, so siblings (dialog buttons, preview) cannot reach it. Correct lifts the state into a Provider that wraps the dialog. The regex only looks at a *Composer() with no parameters; a different shape may pass falsely.
